Depends on what you're developing. You do not necessarily need to be developing for/on Windows 10 explicitly. I don't know what your requirements are that mandate that you must develop on Windows 10 and can't have your developer machines on Windows 7, but for most applications you probably don't need that unless work is forcing you to. Now "most" does not mean "all," so you may be one of the unlucky few, but nevertheless, it isn't necessary most of the time. AFAIK most developer tools for Windows are still supported on Windows 7 (begrudgingly though it may be at this point, at least for Microsoft's tools). So that leaves the software being developed requiring Windows 10, presumably without the benefit of dedicated testing machines. Custom software may require being developed specifically for Windows 10 (although I seriously question any custom software that is developed on top of Windows 10 with it being the sole and only targeted platform). However, more general-purpose, public software probably does not have that requirement. In fact, I would be wary of any software that does not work on Windows 7 at this point, it certainly isn't THAT old, my opinions of Windows 7 vs. 10 put aside entirely. Now testing probably does need Windows 10, but test machines are a lot different than general development machines in most cases, in my experience, and may often be isolated from the network in any case.

Second, however, you can run Windows 10 in a virtual machine if you'd like, and if you've got things set up decently in Linux you can probably make it run pretty decently. Although I have never tried, I've seen it optimized in VirtualBox to run at near-native speeds, which should be plenty for most purposes. While this will not in and of itself save your machine from an update, it leaves the machine itself free, and the possibility of starting up another instance isolated from the Internet or something along those lines.

Note that I am not trying to belittle whatever your situation is that requires you to use Windows 10, but I do think there may be options that you may wish to reconsider, some of which aren't very obvious, and others that other people might want to consider should they be faced with a similar situation.
The only reason to require W10 for development, that I can come up with, is DX12.
